hist.island-core: Named by the Eastern Shoals Company for those lost on the passage. The name was never revised by any later administration.
hist.island-ne: Absent from the current civic register. Older charts give a name the present administration does not use.
hist.island-nw: Retains a customs exemption dating to the Company concession. The exemption was never formally closed.
hist.island-sw: Renamed by the Republic for the residents it expects. The earlier Protectorate name, Concord, is no longer in administrative use.
hist.island-se: The name in current administrative use. An earlier name remains in circulation on charts from the other claimant.
hist.site-re-1:
Four fingers made from ruin reaching into the sky
a skeletal hand, victim of unknown conflict
a site for a communion ungrasped
a gesture from a time unremembered
a fifth finger excised.

The central landmark of Remembrance, the Void is a sacred, taboo site for both the Republic and the Remembered. Each believes it to be the location of a key battle during the war of the Redaction. Neither can recall its significance, nor what structures stood there before.
hist.site-re-2:
The Watchtower stands as a pointed finger
Beckoning towards distant shores or
Ostracizing those who linger
A cypher once stood here, now unmade and unread.
One hand waves ships in. The same hand waves them off.

This lone watchtower is Remembrance's oldest structure, raised soon after the Company's charting to watch the channel for incoming vessels. Built over a now-lost Lanting monument, the tower now maintains two crews, each operating different shifts using different stairways for entry. The Republic crews control immigration, and observe and welcome new immigrants from the Interzone, while a Remembered team covertly controls expulsion, marking those to be driven out.
hist.site-ne-2: Across Silence, surrounding the Eye, hushed buildings lie squat. Remembered prisoners live within these cells, those who refuse to listen to the new Language. They are counted each morning and left in the dark each night, when a few windows are lit in undeciphered patterns, changing nightly and never repeated.
hist.site-nw-1:
Its name is the place between
a dark road for the Remembered
a drowned ruin that rises with the tide.
Two brothers raised four islands
A fifth one now held up, awoken

The marshland known to locals as the Low Spaces is built upon Lanting-era megaliths, the burial sites of the islands' mythical founders, a pair of divine snake twins who raised the islands from the sea. Rumoured to be haunted, its impenetrable mangrove serves smugglers as a route: books come in and (___) is carried out.
hist.site-nw-3:
A market grown in the queue for a door
one wall of words that may be said, each meaning only itself
one wall of brackets where the banned ones were
the failed wait here until the waiting is an address
the ones who pass are not seen again

Portside grew in the yard outside the Examination Halls, where candidates who fail the exam wait to sit it again. Kept empty by design and never cleared, since the Interzone's customs exemption leaves no authority able to clear it, it is now a market in dozens of languages, selling coached scripts, forged certificates and interpreters, and taking in books from outside. Two walls face the lane. One lists the words the Republic allows, each set equal to itself; the other holds only empty brackets, since a banned word is never written down.
hist.site-sw-1:
Empty houses await their families
tables set, beds made
in the lit windows, faces
perfectly spoken, perfectly alike
when they settle, nothing more will be said

Homeland was built to house Republic families who never arrived. Children who slip in after dark tell of families already living there. Every child describes them the same way: faces like their own, speaking a language familiar but unrecognised. Adults driving past see only lit windows and empty show homes.
hist.site-se-1: Established to monitor settlement across the archipelago. Its findings are not a matter of public record.
hist.site-se-2: Contractor records, unclaimed after dissolution. Sealed by default, not by order.
hist.site-se-3: Issues consent for construction. Heavy load applications are subject to an unwritten review.
hist.site-se-4: Paired with the station on the Interzone. The pairing is not named in either island's charter.
hist.span-a: Checkpointed at both landings since construction. No alternate route between the outer islands exists.
hist.span-b: Rebuilt after a partial failure. The replacement span is a different width from the original deck.
hist.span-c: Held under private concession. Its posted load limit is lower than its rated capacity.
hist.span-d: Carries a telemetry conduit alongside the roadway, installed after the deck itself.
hist.site-ne-1:
A tower that sings in one language
a voice once loved, all day, all night
each word meaning only itself
it asks you to come home
below, they answer in the gaps

The Eye stands in the clearing at the centre of Silence, a fenced broadcast tower ringed with loudspeaker horns. It plays Language without pause: announcements, lessons and songs, sung by a voice no one on the island can name. The broadcasts predate everyone now held here, and no record states who they were first meant for. The detained answer in (___), which the horns cannot carry.
hist.site-sw-2:
A garden laid on borrowed soil
birds return to a place that is gone
calling a name no one can read
the grown hear only birdsong
the children stop and answer

Laid on reclaimed reef, a Republic botanical garden no one visits. Salt rises through the imported soil and the lawns are reseeded every season. Each year migratory birds land where the reef once was, calling a single word, zauran. Gardeners chase them off as pests. Children who hear it stop and call back, and the Remembered who hear it cannot say why they remember.

site-re-1.t: Every causeway on this island ends here. But nobody lives there?
Yeah nobody lives there, everyone just passes through it.
I've been doing some research, but it just turns up as a gap in the history.
Don't you think it's strange that both the Republic and the Remembered date their formation to this, but no one knows what it is?
Everyone agrees it was a war. Nobody agrees who was fighting.
Ask any of the locals, they'll tell you there's a fifth but we aren't supposed to talk about it.

Did you know some cultures believe the number 4 to be unlucky? Some buildings even skip that level. But it makes sense in engineering — a cube frame seems stable, but unless you introduce a fifth line diagonally, the whole thing falls apart.
We have a word for that in our language, both for the void and the hidden force that holds up the world. We call it (___).
Is that your word for a hole with a shape?
... It's the only one I've got.

site-re-2.t: Satellite images log it as an immigration post, but it looks pretty strange from here.
Yes — also, research indicates it's built on top of an old Lanting monument. A harbour marker of some kind.

Hmm... my grandmother used to say it was two winding snakes. But nowadays the Republic and the Remembered use both entries for different purposes. The Republic to monitor the right kind of people in, and the Remembered to keep foreigners out.
Snakes.... SNAAKKKE... sorry, I hate snakes.

Just like... the Double Helix, right? It's everywhere once you start looking — caduceus, ouroboros pairs, twin serpents wound around a staff. DNA itself, obviously. Something about two things spiraling around each other and never quite touching keeps showing up whenever people try to draw two forces that are opposed and inseparable at the same time.

site-ne-2.t: It's quieter here. The feed's almost clear.
Thick walls. They don't want the prisoners speaking to each other.
They do, don't they? The prisoners use them to talk. A code of dots and dashes.
Like Morse. Did you know prisoners of war in Vietnam talked through their cell walls by tapping? Five rows, five columns, a letter in every square.
They dropped the K and used C instead. They had to lose a letter to make the language fit the walls.

site-nw-1.t: The chart shows a tidal flat here. Satellite images show boats coming in and out.
Boats go a lot of places.
Sorry, I'm just trying to understand the smuggling route. That's a lot of mangrove to be nothing.

site-nw-3.t: The left wall is just blanks. How does anyone know what's banned?
Some time ago, something happened that nobody can agree on. We call it the Redaction. It took away ideas, words, thoughts. The Republic tries to index what is missing and build new words for them.
So people allowed in can only enter if they speak the standardized language?
Yes. But what they don't know is that we can still speak (___). It (___) just (___) stopped (___) being (___) written (___) down.
Wait. Something's wrong. Rawi, did you do something?

site-sw-1.t: There are families everywhere. In every window.
Did you know Henry Ford once built a Michigan town in the Amazon? Lawns, square dances, American food in the canteen. He called it Fordlândia.
Nobody. The workers rioted over the canteen, the rubber died, and the jungle started taking it back.
Some are still standing. Other people live in them now.
There's one at the window. He looks like you.

site-se-1.t: The office that keeps the islands level. That is the whole of the public description.
Statutory remit: detect and correct differential settlement. Actual function: hold the coupling data and decline to publish.
Nobody I know has been inside.
It is the only body that could prove the pairing, and the only one that will not.

site-se-2.t: The old papers. Lost in a merger, they say, and nobody has ever named the company.
Original contractor records. Proprietary when filed, unclaimed after dissolution, sealed by default rather than by decision.
A story that has been told the same way for forty years.
Not a conspiracy. An absence that nobody had standing to fill.

site-se-3.t: You may build. The question is whether you may build heavy.
Load consent issued here, silently checked against the paired island\u2019s current settlement figure.
Light construction, no trouble. Heavy, and the file goes quiet.
The check is not written into any statute I can find.

site-se-4.t: Its twin is across the water. Children are told they are talking to each other.
Paired inclinometer to the Interzone station. This pairing is what the folk account describes correctly and explains wrongly.
A nice story. It happens to be true.
They got the mechanism right and lost the reason. That is usually the order.

span-a.t: You do not walk this one for pleasure. There is one reason to be on it, in either direction.
Single carriageway, checkpointed both landings. Every span terminates on Remembrance, so nothing moves between outer islands without passing through it.
There is no route between two outer islands. By design.

span-b.t: The newcomers\u2019 road. Widened twice and still not wide enough.
Highest-volume span. Rebuilt after partial collapse; the replacement deck is a different width and the join is visible.
Everything that arrives here crosses it eventually.
No collapse appears in any record I have access to.

span-c.t: Quiet, well kept, and busier than it looks.
Privately maintained under concession. Load-restricted — stated as a deck limit, actually a ballast limit.
The gate is open. It is simply never used by us.
A deck that grade could carry three times the posted figure.

span-d.t: Administrative link carrying the tilt telemetry conduit beside the roadway. The conduit is why the footing is oversized.
Two lanes of forms, going both ways.
The data crosses. The findings never do.

site-ne-1.t: Is that feed live? I can barely hear you.
Same songs, on loop, forever. It stays with you, no?
Why do they do it? Some kind of torture? Brainwashing?
A love song can be torture sometimes, I guess. But it's about Language.
Listen to the chorus. What is she asking for?

site-sw-2.t: Birds. Hundreds of them, all over the lawns.
Every year. They come for the reef.
Zauran. It's what we call them.
The last speaker of the Atures language was a parrot. An explorer wrote down what it said. Two centuries later, an artist taught those words to new parrots.
And none of them knew what they were saying.

intro.t: Five reclamations on one engineered seabed. Charted by the Eastern Shoals Company, numbered by the Protectorate, claimed now by two states that do not recognise each other.
Nobody here says it like that. Pick a place off the chart and I will tell you what people say about it.
